column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/caixa-auto-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS PINS. Three jobs: bump -> {ship | publish-withheld}. Four context
# paths appear in an `if:` — github.actor (the bot re-trigger loop guard on
# bump), needs.bump.outputs.bumped (the publish gate), and the pair
# github.event.repository.private + inputs.publish-from-private (the privacy
# guard and its opt-in escape). The table fixes the selected set for every
# combination that can actually occur.
# WHY IT EXISTS. On 2026-08-08 pleme-io/graphql-synthesizer ran the sibling
# cargo-auto-release, reported SUCCESS, bumped + tagged + pushed, and published
# nothing — its ship job carried `&& !github.event.repository.private` and was
# silently skipped. A deliberate no-publish and a broken no-publish were the
# same green tick, because nobody had written down which jobs must run.
# ── ROW 2 REVERSED ON 2026-08-17. READ THIS BEFORE CHANGING IT BACK. ────────
# This header used to argue at length that the absence of a privacy guard here
# was deliberate, and row 2 asserted that a private caixa repo PUBLISHES. The
# argument was that caixa-publish pushes to our own OCI registry rather than a
# public index, so a private repo shipping a private artifact is the correct
# outcome. That reasoning is still sound about the DESTINATION and is preserved
# below — what changed is that "correct outcome" and "silent default" are not
# the same thing, and only the first was ever argued for.
# The measurement behind the reversal (2026-08-17, org's 384 container
# packages): the `helm/*` namespace holds exactly one package,
# `helm/pangea-operator`, and it is INTERNAL; chart packages org-wide run 186
# internal / 6 private / 15 public. So the disclosure risk is genuinely low —
# ghcr.io has a real private/internal tier and a GHCR version can be deleted
# outright, so NEITHER clause of the generic guard's rationale ("leaks source to
# a public registry", "cannot be withdrawn, only yanked") holds here. This guard
# buys FAMILY-WIDE CONSISTENCY plus a cheap belt on the one real residual:
# nothing in this path pins the created package's visibility, and those 15
# public chart packages prove a public one is constructible in this org.
# What makes adding the guard safe rather than a re-run of the graphql-
# synthesizer defect is that it ANNOUNCES ITSELF. publish-withheld is ship's
# exact complement over the bumped case, so exactly one of the two selects
# whenever a bump happened, and a withheld publish emits a ::notice + a step
# summary instead of an absence. Rows 2 and 3 assert both halves of that
# partition.
# CONSEQUENCE FOR CONSUMERS, stated so it is not discovered by surprise: a
# private caixa repo that legitimately ships a private chart to our own registry
# — which, per the measurement above, is the NORMAL case here rather than a rare
# exception — must now set `publish-from-private: true`. That is one line in the
# caller, and it converts an unexamined default into a stated intent.
# inputs.publish-from-private is declared in EVERY row, including the public
# ones where no `if:` outcome turns on it: an undeclared context path is an
# ERROR by design, because a case that models a scenario while leaving a path it
# does not mention to default silently is how a table drifts out from under its
# workflow. always() is declared for the same reason — publish-withheld's
# condition reads it.
# 1. The happy path on a public repo: a bump publishes, and nothing is withheld.
public-bump-publishes
# 2. THE GUARD FIRING, AND SAYING SO. A private repo without the opt-in
#    publishes nothing — and publish-withheld RUNS, so the skip is a statement
#    rather than an absence. This row previously asserted the opposite; see the
#    header for why it reversed and why that is not a regression to the
#    silent-skip defect.
private-bump-withheld
# 3. THE ESCAPE HATCH, and for this workflow the expected setting on a private
#    caixa repo: opting in restores publishing and stands the notice down.
private-bump-opt-in
# 4. Nothing to release: bump runs and finds no change, so ship must not fire.
#    This is the case that keeps ship's condition from being weakened to
#    always(). publish-withheld stays quiet too — nothing was withheld, there
#    was simply nothing to publish.
public-no-bump
# 5. The bot's own commit-and-push must not re-trigger the pipeline. bump is
#    skipped by the actor guard; ship is skipped both by its own condition and by
#    needs-propagation. The empty value models a SKIPPED upstream job, which is a
#    distinct state from 'false' — bump never ran, so it emitted no output at all.
#    publish-withheld skips on bumped != 'true' DESPITE its always(), which is
#    what keeps the bot loop from emitting a spurious withheld notice.
#    NOTE, measured 2026-08-17: this row does NOT hold publish-withheld's
#    always() clause. Removing always() keeps all 5 rows green, because bump
#    skipping here leaves bumped EMPTY and the condition is already false. The
#    case always() actually covers — bump FAILING after setting bumped=true — is
#    outside this oracle, which models job SELECTION and not job SUCCESS. Stated
#    so nobody reads the green table as evidence for that clause.
bot-actor-no-loop
